The debug build now trusts the dev server's self-signed certificate, so the `Trust anchor for certification path not found` error should go away. I couldn't build or run the app here, so this is verified by reading the files only.

**Cause:** The debug build calls `https://10.0.2.2:8443/`, which the docker dev server serves with the self-signed certificate in `dev-ca/shelftap-dev-ca.pem`. Android doesn't trust that certificate, so the TLS handshake fails.

**Changes**, all in the debug source set so release builds are unaffected:

- `app/src/debug/res/raw/shelftap_dev_ca.pem`: a copy of the dev certificate, which is a single self-signed cert.
- `app/src/debug/res/xml/network_security_config.xml`: a config that trusts the system CAs plus the dev certificate.
- `app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml`: a manifest overlay that sets `android:networkSecurityConfig` on the application. It merges into the debug variant only.

I didn't touch `CatalogClient.kt` or disable certificate validation anywhere. The release build still uses normal validation against `api.shelftap.example`.

**Choices I made:**
- I copied the PEM into the project rather than pointing at `dev-ca/`, because Android resources must live under `res/`.
- I kept the system CAs in the trust anchors, so debug builds still accept normal HTTPS hosts.

If the dev certificate is ever regenerated, the `shelftap_dev_ca.pem` copy has to be updated to match. The old one will stop working.
